content.content:
1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison) queries, the reservation/alert listings,
85	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
86	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
87	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`, and the other
88	  read-only branch entry points.
89	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
90	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
91	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
92	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
93	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
94	
95	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
96	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
97	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
98	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
99	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
100	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
101	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
102	is `403`, never `404`.
103	
104	## Event ledger
105	
106	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
107	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
108	
109	### `POST /events`
110	
111	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
112	exactly these five top-level fields:
113	
114	| Field          | Rule                                      |
115	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
116	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
117	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
118	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
119	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
120	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
121	
122	```bash
123	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
124	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
125	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
126	```
127	
128	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
129	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
130	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
131	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
132	  the other fields differ.
133	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
134	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
135	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
136	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
137	
138	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
139	
140	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
141	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
142	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
143	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
144	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
145	
146	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
147	
148	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
149	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
150	organizations' data is never included.
151	
152	Query parameters:
153	
154	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
155	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
156	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
157	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
158	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
159	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
160	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
161	
162	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
163	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
164	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
165	
166	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
167	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
168	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
169	
170	```json
171	{
172	  "organizationId": "org-1",
173	  "type": "incident.created",
174	  "windowSize": 60,
175	  "from": null,
176	  "to": null,
177	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
178	}
179	```
180	
181	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
182	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
183	  `windows` is `[]`.
184	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
185	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
186	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
187	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
188	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
189	
190	```bash
191	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
192	```
193	
194	### Region attribution
195	
196	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
197	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
198	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
199	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
200	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
201	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
202	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
203	
204	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
205	
206	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
207	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
208	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
209	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
210	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
211	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
212	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
213	point and a trailing newline.
214	
215	```bash
216	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
217	```
218	
219	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
220	
221	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
222	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
223	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
224	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
225	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
226	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
227	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
228	newline):
229	
230	```json
231	{
232	  "organizationId": "org-1",
233	  "region": "north",
234	  "type": "incident.created",
235	  "windowSize": 60,
236	  "from": null,
237	  "to": null,
238	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
239	}
240	```
241	
242	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
243	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
244	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
245	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
246	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
247	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
248	
249	```bash
250	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
251	```
252	
253	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
254	
255	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
256	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
257	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
258	object containing exactly these fields:
259	
260	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
261	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
262	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
263	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
264	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
265	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
266	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
267	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
268	
269	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
270	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
271	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
272	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
273	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
274	ones for audit reconciliation.
275	
276	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
277	
278	```json
279	{
280	  "organizationId": "org-1",
281	  "type": "incident.created",
282	  "windowSize": 60,
283	  "from": null,
284	  "to": null,
285	  "peakStart": 60,
286	  "peakCount": 2,
287	  "action": "observe"
288	}
289	```
290	
291	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
292	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
293	  regardless of event submission order.
294	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
295	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
296	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
297	  `"observe"`.
298	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
299	  other organizations' data is never included.
300	
301	```bash
302	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
303	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
304	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
305	```
306	
307	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
308	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
309	  produced.
310	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
311	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
312	
313	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
314	
315	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
316	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
317	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
318	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
319	exactly these fields:
320	
321	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
322	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
323	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
324	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
325	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
326	
327	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
328	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
329	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
330	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
331	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
332	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
333	
334	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
335	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
336	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
337	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
338	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
339	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
340	demands.
341	
342	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
343	
344	```json
345	{
346	  "organizationId": "org-1",
347	  "assignments": [
348	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
349	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
350	  ],
351	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
352	  "totalUnits": 6
353	}
354	```
355	
356	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
357	  processing order.
358	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
359	  `demandId`.
360	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
361	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
362	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
363	
364	```bash
365	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
366	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
367	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
368	```
369	
370	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
371	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
372	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
373	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
374	
375	## Reservation inventory
376	
377	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
378	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
379	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
380	is never rewritten afterwards.
381	
382	### `POST /reservations`
383	
384	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
385	with exactly these five top-level fields:
386	
387	| Field           | Rule                                      |
388	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
389	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
390	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
391	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
392	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
393	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
394	
395	```bash
396	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
397	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
398	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
399	```
400	
401	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
402	and a trailing newline:
403	
404	```json
405	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
406	```
407	
408	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
409	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
410	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
411	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
412	
413	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
414	  resource also establishes its capacity.
415	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
416	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
417	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
418	  exists but the other fields differ.
419	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
420	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
421	  capacity is never rewritten.
422	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
423	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
424	  unchanged.
425	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
426	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
427	  is produced.
428	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
429	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
430	
431	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
432	
433	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
434	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
435	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
436	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
437	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
438	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
439	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
440	`422`.
441	
442	## Alert suppression and escalation
443	
444	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
445	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
446	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
447	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
448	paths are added.
449	
450	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
451	
452	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
453	containing exactly these fields:
454	
455	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
456	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
457	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
458	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
459	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
460	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
461	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
462	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
463	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
464	
465	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
466	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
467	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
468	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
469	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
470	
471	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
472	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
473	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
474	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
475	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
476	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
477	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
478	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
479	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
480	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
481	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
482	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
483	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
484	    organization/type always creates an alert.
485	
486	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
487	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
488	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
489	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
490	trailing newline):
491	
492	```json
493	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
494	```
495	
496	```bash
497	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
498	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
499	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
500	```
501	
502	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
503	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
504	  written.
505	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
506	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
507	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
508	
509	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
510	
511	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
512	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
513	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
514	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
515	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
516	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
517	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
518	
519	## Snapshots and branches
520	
521	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
522	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
523	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
524	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
525	the main service or with other branches.
526	
527	### Organization boundaries
528	
529	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
530	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
531	scoped to that boundary:
532	
533	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
534	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
535	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
536	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
537	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
538	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
539	  organization's data never changes them.
540	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
541	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
542	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
543	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
544	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
545	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
546	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
547	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
548	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
549	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
550	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
551	  namespaced per organization.
552	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
553	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
554	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
555	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
556	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
557	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
558	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
559	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
560	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
561	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
562	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
563	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
564	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
565	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
566	
567	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
568	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
569	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
570	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
571	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.
572	
573	### `POST /snapshots`
574	
575	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
576	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
577	
578	| Field        | Rule                     |
579	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
580	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
581	
582	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
583	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
584	JSON:
585	
586	```json
587	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
588	```
589	
590	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
591	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
592	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
593	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
594	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
595	  content is never replaced or mutated.
596	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
597	  organization; no snapshot is stored.
598	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
599	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
600	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, a missing or extra field,
601	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.
602	- Any failed request leaves both the main state and existing snapshots
603	  unchanged.
604	
605	### `GET /snapshots`
606	
607	Returns `200` with `{"snapshots": [...]}`, listing **only the caller
608	organization's** snapshots; other organizations' snapshots are never visible.
609	Each entry has the same shape as a creation response, and entries are sorted
610	by `snapshotId` in Unicode code-point order. With no snapshots the collection
611	is an empty array.
612	
613	### `POST /branches`
614	
615	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
616	must be a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
617	
618	| Field        | Rule                     |
619	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
620	| `branchId`   | non-empty string         |
621	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
622	
623	The new branch receives independent copies of the snapshot's events,
624	resource capacities, and reservation balances (which hold only the snapshot
625	owner organization's data).
626	
627	- `201 Created` — the branch summary is returned:
628	
629	```json
630	{"branchId":"br-1","events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
631	```
632	
633	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the named snapshot exists but
634	  belongs to another organization (ownership is checked before the branch
635	  name), or the credential is read-only. No branch is created and no snapshot
636	  content is returned.
637	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — no snapshot with that
638	  name has ever existed; no branch is created.
639	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "branch_conflict"}`) — the snapshot is owned by
640	  the caller but a branch with that `branchId` already exists anywhere in the
641	  service. The existing branch is unaffected.
642	- `415`, `400`, and `422` follow the same rules as other JSON write
643	  endpoints; `422` (`validation_error`) covers missing, extra, blank, or
644	  non-string fields.
645	
646	### `GET /branches/{branchId}`
647	
648	Returns `200` with the branch summary (see above) when the branch belongs to
649	the caller's organization. A branch owned by another organization returns
650	`403` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and no content. Only a branch name that
651	has never existed returns `404` with `{"error": "branch_not_found"}`.
652	
653	### Branch-prefixed entry points
654	
655	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
656	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
657	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
658	
659	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
660	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
661	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | list the branch's events                  |
662	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events/aggregate`   | aggregate the branch's events             |
663	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | commit an event into the branch only      |
664	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/decisions/evaluate` | evaluate against the branch's events only |
665	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | list the branch's reservations            |
666	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | reserve against branch balances only      |
667	
668	- Branch event commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, identical-replay (`200`),
669	  and `event_id_conflict` (`409`); writes stay in the branch. Name and
670	  capacity comparisons run only against the owning organization's records
671	  that were forked into the branch, so another organization's event
672	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never trigger a
673	  conflict and never affect a branch balance.
674	- Branch reservation commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, and the replay and
675	  capacity rules: identical replays return `200` without double counting,
676	  while `reservation_conflict`, `capacity_conflict`, and
677	  `capacity_exceeded` still return `409`; a failed commit never changes the
678	  branch inventory.
679	- Branch list and aggregate queries apply the same parameter rules as the
680	  main endpoints; missing, duplicated, or empty parameters return `422` with
681	  `validation_error`.
682	- Branch evaluation is read-only over branch events, and branch aggregates
683	  never count main-service events; repeated identical requests return
684	  identical results.
685	- No branch operation creates or rolls back main-service state, and branches
686	  never observe each other's writes. Unknown sub-paths under a known branch
687	  return the standard JSON `404`; sub-paths under an unknown branch return
688	  `branch_not_found`.
689	- The region queries (`/events/region` and `/events/region/aggregate`) are
690	  main-only; no branch-prefixed region paths are added.
691	- `/decisions/allocate` remains a main-only, stateless endpoint.
692	
693	### `POST /branches/compare`
694	
695	A read-only comparison of two existing branches' window counts and peak
696	decisions. Each side recomputes its window counts and peak from that
697	branch's own events only; nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or
698	in the main service is read for mutation or written, and identical
699	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
700	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
701	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
702	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
703	
704	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
705	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
706	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
707	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
708	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
709	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
710	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
711	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
712	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
713	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
714	
715	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
716	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
717	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
718	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
719	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
720	
721	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
722	  hit by matching events on either side, aligned row-by-row by `start`
723	  ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's count as
724	  `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
725	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
726	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
727	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
728	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
729	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
730	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
731	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
732	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
733	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
734	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
735	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
736	
737	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
738	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
739	newline:
740	
741	```json
742	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"br-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"br-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
743	```
744	
745	```bash
746	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare \
747	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
748	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
749	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
750	```
751	
752	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
753	  registered.
754	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
755	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
756	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
757	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
758	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
759	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
760	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
761	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
762	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
763	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
764	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
765	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`left`/
766	  `right`/`type`, non-positive-integer `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or
767	  non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
768	
769	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
770	branch and changes no event, reservation, or decision state.
771	
772	### `POST /branches/compare/events`
773	
774	A read-only, event-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
775	`POST /branches/compare` aligns window counts, this entry point aligns the
776	two branches' events by `eventId` and reports the deterministic difference
777	summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or in the main
778	service is read for mutation or written, and identical submissions return
779	byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call
780	it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound
781	to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object
782	containing exactly these fields:
783	
784	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
785	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
786	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
787	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
788	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
789	
790	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
791	are then equal by construction and every shared event lands in `same`.
792	
793	Events are aligned by `eventId`:
794	
795	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
796	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
797	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose events are identical in every
798	  field except `eventId`; payloads compare by content, so key order inside
799	  a payload never matters.
800	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides whose events disagree. Each entry is
801	  `{"eventId", "fields"}`, where `fields` names the mismatched fields
802	  (drawn from `organizationId`, `type`, `occurredAt`, `payload`).
803	
804	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
805	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
806	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
807	neither branch holds any event, all four groups are empty arrays and all
808	four counts are `0`.
809	
810	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
811	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
812	
813	```json
814	{"diff":[{"eventId":"evt-2","fields":["occurredAt","payload"]}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["evt-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["evt-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["evt-3"],"sameCount":1}
815	```
816	
817	```bash
818	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare/events \
819	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
820	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
821	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b"}'
822	```
823	
824	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
825	  registered.
826	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
827	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
828	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
829	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
830	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
831	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
832	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
833	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
834	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
835	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
836	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
837	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
838	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
839	
840	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
841	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
842	
843	### `POST /branches/compare/reservations`
844	
845	A read-only, reservation-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
846	`POST /branches/compare/events` aligns events by `eventId`, this entry point
847	aligns the two branches' reservations by `reservationId` and reports the
848	deterministic difference summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other
849	branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or written, alert state
850	is untouched, and identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
851	Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. Requires
852	`Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the
853	request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object containing
854	exactly these fields:
855	
856	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
857	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
858	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
859	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
860	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
861	
862	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
863	are then equal by construction and every shared reservation lands in
864	`same`.
865	
866	Reservations are aligned by `reservationId`:
867	
868	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
869	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
870	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose `organizationId`, `resourceId`,
871	  `quantity`, and `capacity` all match.
872	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides that disagree in at least one of those
873	  four fields. Each entry is `{"reservationId", "fields"}`, where `fields`
874	  names the mismatched fields, drawn only from `organizationId`,
875	  `resourceId`, `quantity`, and `capacity`; no other content participates
876	  in the comparison.
877	
878	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
879	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
880	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
881	neither branch holds any reservation for the organization, all four groups
882	are empty arrays and all four counts are `0`.
883	
884	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
885	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
886	
887	```json
888	{"diff":[{"fields":["capacity","quantity"],"reservationId":"res-2"}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["res-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["res-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["res-3"],"sameCount":1}
889	```
890	
891	```bash
892	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare/reservations \
893	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
894	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
895	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b"}'
896	```
897	
898	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
899	  registered.
900	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
901	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
902	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
903	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
904	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
905	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
906	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
907	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
908	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
909	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
910	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
911	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
912	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
913	
914	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
915	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
916
